assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes; daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready.

## Which scenario this is

2.17 "user-blocking-question" is the PLAIN QUESTION TO THE USER scenario — the agent's own reply text ends in a question mark, exercising `session.IsWaitingForUserInput`'s trailing-? path (`state_classifier.go`'s `classifyAgentDone` branch, the scenario's own description calls it "decision 2a"). It is NOT the permission/approval-prompt scenario: claudecode's sibling cells split these explicitly (`2-17_user-blocking-question` vs `2-18_user-blocking-plan-mode-approval`), and muse itself has a structurally separate `kind:"approval"` flow (format-spec §5) that a different, already-assessed cell covers. This assessment judges the trailing-? path only.

## Agent

Muse ships a dedicated `request_user_input` tool, declared active in every real session's toolset (muse-format-spec.md §5, `model_request_configured.toolset.active_tools`), and the shipped binary's own system prompt explicitly steers the model toward it: `strings ~/.local/bin/muse-bin-1.2.1-R2847.1 | grep -i request_user_input` (run this session) turns up the literal instruction "5. Prefer `request_user_input` when available. Ask one blocking outcome question;". That raised a real question: would a naive "ask a clarifying question" prompt actually produce the trailing-? PROSE path this scenario needs, or would the model reach for the tool instead (whose wire shape — `userInput/request`/`userInput/requested`, carrying the question inside structured `questions[]` params, per `muse schema generate-json-schema`'s `msp.schema.json` — was never once observed invoked in the underlying 14-session corpus, muse-format-spec.md §12)?

I settled this empirically instead of guessing. `assistant_message_committed` (arbitrary free-text replies, no tool involved) is already one of the ~19 real event kinds the corpus census found in a single clean session tree (muse-format-spec.md §3) — plain conversational replies are ordinary for muse, not a corner case — and I live-drove it directly: launched `muse --trust-workspace` interactively in tmux (mirroring `driver-interactive.sh`'s `launch_repl`) and sent "Before doing anything else, ask me exactly one clarifying question about which output format I want, then stop and wait for my answer. Do not use any tools yet." The resulting real session (`~/.local/share/muse/sessions/2026/09/14/01a09d9c-58d4-7ae0-b533-88a6fd2fa008/session.jsonl`) contains exactly one `assistant_message_committed` — `{"text":"Which output format would you like me to use?"}` — immediately followed by `{"kind":"terminal","terminal":"completed"}`, with NO `assistant_tool_calls_committed` and NO `kind:"approval"` record anywhere in that run. An explicit "don't use tools" instruction reliably steers muse onto the plain-text path — the same lever mistral-vibe's own already-assessed 2.17 recipe already uses for the identical shape (dedicated ask-tool + free-text fallback). agent_supports=yes rests on this live-confirmed capability, not a doc guess.

## Daemon

`core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go:428-438` (`parseAssistantMessageCommitted`) surfaces the reply as `ev.AssistantText` and computes `ev.PendingWaitingCue = session.ProseIndicatesWaiting(tailer.WaitingScanWindow(text))` — the same general mechanism every other already-observed cell in this scenario column relies on (claudecode, codex, copilot, gemini-cli, hermes, kiro-cli, mistral-vibe, pi all carry `daemon_capability:full` for this exact scenario per `of status --scenario user-blocking-question`). I did not stop at reading the wiring: I fed the REAL captured line from the live probe above through the actual `(&Parser{}).ParseLine` this session (a throwaway `_test.go`, removed afterward — not committed) and confirmed `EventType="assistant_message"`, `PendingWaitingCue=true`, `Skip=false`. `parser.go:324-326` (`parseRunTerminal`) sets `EventType="turn_done"` on muse's `terminal` event for all three outcomes (completed/cancelled/failed), which is exactly the probe's very next record (`terminal:"completed"`) — so `SessionMetrics.IsAgentDone()` goes true with no open tool call, and `state_classifier.go`'s ladder (permission-prompt-open → `NeedsUserAttention()` → `OpenToolStalled` → `IsAgentDone()` → `classifyAgentDone` → `IsWaitingForUserInput()`) reaches `waiting`, cross-checked directly against `core/application/services/state_classifier.go` (muse-adapter-contract.md §5 summarizes the same ladder). Unit coverage: `TestParseLine_AssistantMessageCommitted_WaitingCue` (parser_test.go:245-255), synthetic but shaped identically to the real capture; the live probe promotes the verdict from "parser looks right" to "parser proven right on real muse 1.2.1 output."

## A real, named, non-load-bearing gap

`request_user_input` — muse's own dedicated ask-tool, the one its system prompt tells the model to prefer — is NOT in the daemon's user-blocking-tool allowlist. Both copies (`core/domain/session/metrics.go:501 isUserBlockingTool`, `core/pkg/tailer/tailer_config.go:46 isUserBlockingToolName`) enumerate only `AskUserQuestion`, `ExitPlanMode`, `question`, `ask_user_question`, `exit_plan_mode`, `ask_user`. If a differently-worded prompt let the model reach for the tool instead of plain text, `NeedsUserAttention()` stays false for the open call. I checked whether any fallback saves this: `OpenToolStalled`'s duration heuristic (`core/domain/session/signal_hold.go:93-124`) does NOT cover it either — that fallback fires "solely for the five names `isPermissionGatedEditTool` matches" (edit/write/multiedit/notebookedit/write_file), and the same comment block explicitly lists `AskUserQuestion`/`ExitPlanMode` among the tools it does NOT cover. So an open `request_user_input` call would have no fallback at all: `HasOpenToolCall=true` vetoes `IsAgentDone()`, the classifier never reaches the trailing-? branch, and the session would read `working` (or eventually a generic idle heuristic) instead of `waiting` — a silent drop of exactly the signal this project exists to surface. This is why the recipe below explicitly instructs "do not call any tools": that phrasing is a load-bearing precondition of this cell, not incidental wording (Vacuous-pass rule). Wiring `request_user_input` into both allowlists (and, if it ever gets a durable on-disk shape, mapping it the way `kind:"approval"` "requested" already is) is a real, concrete follow-up — but it is a code change, out of scope for `assess`, so it is named here for the maintainer rather than decided silently.

## Driver

`send`/`wait_turn`/`sleep` are all genuinely implemented in `replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh`, confirmed by reading the dispatch case block directly via `driver_step_types_from_file` (not a hand-kept manifest) rather than assumed. The driver was proven end-to-end this session in commit `0239a1bd` ("fix(muse): repair the recording driver so it can't record a corrupted pass"): "Every fix is proven live against muse 1.2.1 via tmux, including one full send -> wait_turn -> exit_clean run through the actual driver." No driver gap for this recipe.
caveats: Load-bearing environment/agent-behaviour property (Vacuous-pass rule): the recipe prompt's explicit "do not call any tools" instruction is required to reliably land on the trailing-? prose path this scenario tests. Muse's system prompt (confirmed via binary strings this session) otherwise tells the model to prefer its dedicated `request_user_input` tool for blocking questions, and that tool is NOT in the daemon's isUserBlockingTool/isUserBlockingToolName allowlist and has NO OpenToolStalled fallback either (core/domain/session/metrics.go:501, core/pkg/tailer/tailer_config.go:46, core/domain/session/signal_hold.go:93-124) — so a prompt that omitted this instruction, or a model that ignored it, could silently degrade this cell into an unobserved (stuck-working) wait instead of a green 'waiting' pass. `record` should re-probe this live and flag an observability_correction if the tool path fires instead.

The live probe above used a slightly different prompt wording ("Do not use any tools yet") than the recipe's final wording ("Do not call any tools — answer in plain text only", modeled on mistral-vibe's own already-assessed 2.17 recipe for the identical dedicated-ask-tool-plus-free-text shape) — both instruct the same thing, but the exact recipe wording has not itself been live-probed verbatim; record is what confirms the final wording behaves identically.

Per the claudecode and mistral-vibe sibling specs for this same scenario, the recipe only exercises the ready→working→waiting half of the scenario's acceptance criteria; the resume half (waiting→working→ready after a reply) is intentionally not driven by this recipe, matching the established fleet-wide convention for this cell.

decision_source.kind for muse's SEPARATE approval/permission-prompt flow was only ever "llm_judge" in the underlying corpus (format-spec §5/§12) — irrelevant to this cell (no approval flow is exercised here, only the plain-text path) but noted since it comes from the same evidence doc.

This verdict is grounded in the built adapter's code + a live probe run THIS session, not yet a recorded, `of record`-verified fixture; record is what promotes it from provisional to settled per the standard assess/record split.

sources.note: Real muse 1.2.1 interactive-TUI run (tmux, --trust-workspace) driven with a clarifying-question prompt: one assistant_message_committed ending '?', immediately followed by terminal:"completed", no tool call, no approval record.
parseRunTerminal sets EventType=turn_done on muse's terminal event; parseAssistantMessageCommitted sets PendingWaitingCue via session.ProseIndicatesWaiting(tailer.WaitingScanWindow(text)).

TestParseLine_AssistantMessageCommitted_WaitingCue pins the trailing-? wiring; re-run this session against the REAL captured probe line (throwaway test, not committed) with the same result: PendingWaitingCue=true.
The state-classifier ladder: NeedsUserAttention -> OpenToolStalled -> IsAgentDone -> classifyAgentDone -> IsWaitingForUserInput -> waiting.
isUserBlockingTool / isUserBlockingToolName allowlists do not include muse's request_user_input tool name.

OpenToolStalled fires solely for the five isPermissionGatedEditTool names; AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode (and by the same logic request_user_input) have no fallback at all if the fast NeedsUserAttention path misses them.
System-prompt string "5. Prefer `request_user_input` when available. Ask one blocking outcome question;" — grounds why the recipe must explicitly forbid tool use.

send/wait_turn/sleep step types genuinely implemented (driver_step_types_from_file), proven end-to-end live against muse 1.2.1 via tmux.

preconditions: muse CLI (1.2.1) on PATH and authenticated (muse login)
irrlichd is recording (isolated coexist mode, or --attach against a --record daemon)

The recipe prompt's explicit "do not call any tools" instruction is a load-bearing precondition (see caveats) — it is what keeps the run on the trailing-? prose path instead of muse's system-prompt-preferred request_user_input tool, which the daemon does not yet recognize as user-blocking
No other muse session shares the driven session's fresh UUID/cwd (driver mints a fresh cwd under <staging>/cwd/)
setup: Driver generates a fresh cwd under <staging>/cwd/ and launches `muse --trust-workspace` (dismisses the untrusted-workspace modal — defect #1 fix, commit 0239a1bd — so the first send is not silently dropped)

script.text: Reply with exactly one short clarifying question, ending in a question mark. Do not call any tools — answer in plain text only. No other text.

verify: events.jsonl shows the muse session reach working after the send
events.jsonl shows exactly one state_transition to waiting after the assistant's question-mark reply
events.jsonl shows NO state_transition to ready for this session after the waiting transition (recipe stops in waiting, never replies)

session.jsonl's final kind:"run" assistant_message_committed text ends in '?', with no assistant_tool_calls_committed event in that same run (confirms the plain-text path was taken, not request_user_input)
